title: Long Runs Are Not Just For Marathoners (Jay Johnson)
population: Recreational 5K to marathon runners; author is a former University of Colorado collegiate coach who has coached U.S. national champions
findings: 5K goal: at least five miles on the long run, progressing up to 10 miles for the more serious runner chasing a 5K PR.
10K goal: minimum of seven to eight miles; a serious 10K runner should aim for a maximum of 10 miles.
Half marathon: about 10 miles for a 'just finish' goal, around 16 miles for serious runners; marathon at least 18 miles, up to 22.
No minutes and no percentage of weekly mileage are given; the page shows an updated date of 2 January 2018.
limitations: Coaching opinion; distances only (no time or weekly share); the 5K maximum of 10 miles is for serious recreational runners. Convention, not evidence.
implications: Coach-level ceilings of about 10 miles (roughly 90-100 min at easy pace, estimate) for both 5K and 10K goals are the upper bound for the high-volume tier; engine caps below this are conservative.

The 5-mile floor for 5K (about 45-50 min, estimate) and 7-8 miles for 10K (about 65-80 min, estimate) suggest medium-tier values near 45-60 min for 5K and 60-75 min for 10K; these are the auditor's pace conversions, not stated by the source.
